_comment: Phrases by which a paper announces its own contribution. Data, not code (R6): they differ by discipline and by decade, and a reviewer extends this file rather than the module. Lower-case; matched as substrings of a lower-cased sentence, and also against the ligature-damaged spelling many PDF extractors produce (see _ligature_note).
_ligature_note: Measured 2026-09-13 on financement/refs/ of the BuildingGIS corpus: pymupdf4llm drops the fi and fl ligatures of Elsevier PDFs, so the text reads 'this paper fnds', 'fll this gap', 'the frst study', 'signifcantly'. extract_contributions.py therefore tests each phrase AND its fi->f / fl->f spelling. Write the phrases here in correct English; the damaged spelling is derived.
_provenance: Extended 2026-09-13 after a measured false negative: davis2021upzonings (Land Use Policy 103, 2021, 105347) states its contribution four times and the 2026-09-12 catalogue matched none of them, because every phrase in it was written in the engineering and computer-science idiom ('this paper presents', 'we propose a') and the planning and social-science idiom ('this paper examines', 'to help fill this gap in the literature', 'minimal empirical research to date has examined') was absent. The corpus measure of that day, 72 of 92 papers stating a contribution, is therefore a lower bound and not a measurement.

novelty: to the best of our knowledge
to the best knowledge of the author
to the best of the author
to the best of my knowledge

exclusions._comment: A sentence carrying one of these is boilerplate, never a claim. Measured 2026-09-13: an Elsevier CRediT block ('CRediT authorship contribution statement ... Data curation') and an acknowledgement ('We thank the reviewers ... improve the ... scientific contribution of our work') both carry the word contribution, so a catalogue containing contribution phrases hits them in EVERY Elsevier paper. Excluding the sentence is cheaper and more honest than narrowing the markers until they stop firing.

caps._comment: Bounds on what one paper may return, so a 30-page article cannot flood a report. Chosen, not measured: a contributions paragraph is a handful of sentences, and a sentence under 6 words states nothing while one over 80 is an extraction artefact.
